mainTopic: Was the עולה at הר סיני an עולת ראייה or the עולת תמיד? Which תנאים hold each view, why רבי ישמעאל is removed from the list, and רב חסדא's question about which animals were brought.
overview: The גמרא asks which תנאים hold that the עולה brought at הר סיני was an עולת ראייה, and which hold it was the עולת תמיד. For רבי ישמעאל, the details of the מצוות came only later in the אהל מועד. So it first seems he cannot hold the offering was the תמיד, since the same offering would have gone from not needing הפשט וניתוח to needing them. רבי אלעזר says the laws of the תמיד were said at סיני but it was not brought there. רבי עקיבא says it was brought and never stopped, and he explains the פסוק in עמוס as meaning that only שבט לוי brought it. On the other side, the גמרא brings בית הלל, רבי עקיבא, and רבי יוסי הגלילי, whose ברייתא shows that only the חגיגה existed before the דיבור. Then the גמרא notes that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the desert תמיד really did change from no הפשט וניתוח to needing them, so רבי ישמעאל is taken off the list. רב חסדא asks whether the desert עולות were sheep or bulls. That would matter for the trope of the פסוק or for a vow, and the question ends in תיקו. Finally, the גמרא begins quoting a משנה in פאה about things that have no set measure.

steps.title: General rules at סיני, details later: the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי ישמעאל's view that the details came in the אהל מועד. רבי עקיבא says general rules and details were all said at סיני, repeated in the אהל מועד, and said a third time in ערבות מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי ישמעאל says: General rules were said at Sinai] and the details in the Tent of Meeting. רבי עקיבא says: General rules and details were said at Sinai, repeated in the Tent of Meeting, and said a third time in the plains of Moab.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא with two opinions about when the details of the מצוות were given to משה. This is the source the גמרא will use in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, only the general rules came at סיני and the details came later in the אהל מועד. For רבי עקיבא, every detail was already given at סיני, and it was later repeated twice. So for רבי ישמעאל there was a time when details like how to prepare a קרבן were not yet known.

keyTerms.meaning: General rules, the main outline of a מצוה
Details, the specifics of how a מצוה is done
The Tent of Meeting, the משכן in the desert
The plains of Moab, where משה taught ספר דברים
And were said a third time

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute about when the details were given is what decides whether the offering at סיני could have been the עולת תמיד.

phrases.english: and the details in the Tent of Meeting.
And Rabbi Akiva says:
General rules and details were said at Sinai,
and were repeated in the Tent of Meeting,
and were said a third time in the plains of Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כְּלָלוֹת וּפְרָטוֹת נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: general rules at סיני, details in the אהל מועד. רבי עקיבא: both at סיני, repeated in the אהל מועד and in ערבות מואב.

steps.title: Why רבי ישמעאל cannot hold the Sinai offering was the daily offering
steps.stepSummary: If the offering at סיני had been the עולת תמיד, the same קרבן would first need no הפשט and ניתוח and later need them. That cannot be, so for רבי ישמעאל it must have been an עולת ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that the burnt-offering Israel brought in the desert was the daily burnt-offering, is there anything that at first did not need skinning and cutting, and in the end needs skinning and cutting?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי ישמעאל's view to prove that, in his opinion, the offering at סיני was not the עולת תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the details such as skinning (הפשט) and cutting into pieces (ניתוח) were only taught later in the אהל מועד. So if the offering at סיני had been the תמיד, the same ongoing תמיד would have changed its rules over time, and that makes no sense. It must have been a different, one-time קרבן, an עולת ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind, used to test an idea
The daily burnt-offering brought every morning and afternoon
Skinning the animal
Cutting the animal into its parts
Is there anything, a question that expects the answer 'no'

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real question looking for an answer. It is a way of saying 'that is impossible', and that proves the offering at סיני was not the תמיד in רבי ישמעאל's view.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that the burnt-offering Israel brought in the desert
phrases.notes: This is the עולה brought at הר סיני before the תורה was given.

phrases.english: was the daily burnt-offering,
is there anything
that at first did not need skinning and cutting,
and in the end needs skinning and cutting?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ עוֹלָה שֶׁהִקְרִיבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר עוֹלַת תָּמִיד הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from רבי ישמעאל's view in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל holds the offering at סיני was an עולת ראייה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל's view that the details, including הפשט and ניתוח, were given only in the אהל מועד

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the daily offering was taught at סיני but not brought there
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on the פסוק 'עולת תמיד העשויה בהר סיני' shows that רבי אלעזר holds the rules of the תמיד were said at סיני, but the תמיד itself was not offered there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר, as it was taught: 'A daily burnt-offering that was made at Mount Sinai.' רבי אלעזר says: Its procedures were said at Sinai, but it itself was not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר is a second תנא who holds the offering at סיני was not the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say the תמיד was 'made' at סיני. רבי אלעזר reads it to mean that only its laws were said there. So the עולה brought at סיני must have been a different קרבן, an עולת ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: That was made or done
Its procedures, how it is done
Was offered, was brought on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar —
phrases.notes: The other תנא who holds it was an עולת ראייה is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא:
"A daily burnt-offering that was made at Mount Sinai,"
Rabbi Elazar says:
its procedures were said at Sinai,
but it itself was not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second תנא who holds the same view as רבי ישמעאל.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר holds the offering at סיני was not the עולת תמיד

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the daily offering was brought at סיני and never stopped
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי עקיבא disagrees. The תמיד was offered at סיני and continued without stopping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: It was offered, and it never stopped again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי עקיבא's opposing view: the offering at סיני was the עולת תמיד itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads 'העשויה בהר סיני' literally, so the תמיד was actually brought at סיני. This fits his view from step 1 that all the details, including הפשט and ניתוח, were already given at סיני. So for him the rules of the תמיד never changed.

keyTerms.meaning: And it never stopped again

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: It was offered,
and it never stopped again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא as רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולת תמיד was offered at סיני and continued without stopping.

steps.title: A verse in עמוס challenges רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how רבי עקיבא explains the פסוק in עמוס that suggests ישראל did not bring קרבנות during their forty years in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain: 'Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings in the desert forty years, house of Israel?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges רבי עקיבא from a פסוק. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said the תמיד never stopped. But the נביא עמוס speaks as if ישראל did not bring קרבנות in the מדבר for forty years. That seems to contradict רבי עקיבא, so he needs to explain the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain, how does this פסוק fit
Did you bring near, did you offer

phrases.english: But how do I explain
"Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings
in the desert forty years, house of Israel?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's claim from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that the תמיד was offered without stopping from סיני onward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in עמוס suggests ישראל did not bring קרבנות during the forty years in the מדבר, which seems to contradict 'it never stopped.'

steps.title: Only the tribe of Levi brought the תמיד in the desert
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the question from עמוס. שבט לוי, who did not serve עבודה זרה, brought the תמיד, so the פסוק can say the rest of ישראל did not bring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tribe of Levi, who did not worship idols, were the ones who offered it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 5. It explains how רבי עקיבא can hold that the תמיד never stopped, even though עמוס says ישראל did not bring קרבנות in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד really was brought the whole time, but it was brought by שבט לוי, who stayed loyal during the עגל. The rest of ישראל, who sinned with עבודה זרה, did not take part, so the פסוק in עמוס speaks about them. This keeps רבי עקיבא's view that the תמיד continued without stopping.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribe of לוי
Idol worship (here, the sin of the עגל)
They offered (a קרבן)

phrases.english: The tribe of Levi
who did not worship idols,
they offered it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the עולת תמיד. So the פסוק in עמוס is talking about everyone else, who did not bring it.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, the תמיד never stopped in the מדבר. שבט לוי kept bringing it, and the פסוק in עמוס refers to the rest of ישראל.
steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי שֶׁלֹּא עָבְדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from עמוס raised in step 5 against רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits who the פסוק is talking about: the rest of ישראל, not שבט לוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in עמוס seems to say no one brought קרבנות for forty years, which would mean the תמיד stopped.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבט לוי brought the תמיד the whole time. The פסוק refers only to those who served עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Sources for בית הלל and רבי עקיבא: what we already said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now lists the sources for those who hold the עולה at סיני was the תמיד. For בית הלל and רבי עקיבא, it points back to what was already explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל: the source is what we said before. רבי עקיבא: the source is also what we said before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new list: the sources for each opinion that holds the עולה at סיני was the עולת תמיד. For the first two names, it simply says we already showed this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא brought sources for the view that the עולה at סיני was an עולת ראייה. Now it turns to the other side. בית הלל's source was explained earlier in the סוגיא, and רבי עקיבא's source is the ברייתא we just learned, where he says the תמיד was offered at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל
That which we said (pointing back to an earlier source)
Also

phrases.english: Beis Hillel: that which we said.
Rabbi Akiva: also that which we said.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 4, where רבי עקיבא says the תמיד was offered at סיני.

steps.confusionAlert: The side has switched. Earlier the sources were for the view that the עולה at סיני was a ראייה. From here on, the sources are for the view that it was the תמיד.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the sources for the ראייה view, the גמרא turns to the sources for the תמיד view.
steps.raayaObject: That בית הלל and רבי עקיבא hold the עולה at סיני was the תמיד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Earlier discussion in the sugya (בית הלל) and the ברייתא of רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר (step 4).

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: three מצוות on the רגל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says ישראל had three מצוות when they went up for the festival: ראייה, חגיגה, and שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי: as a ברייתא teaches. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: ישראל were commanded three מצוות when they went up for the festival: ראייה, חגיגה, and שמחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי. This line sets up the ברייתא by listing the three festival מצוות it will compare next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this is only a list of the three מצוות. The actual proof about סיני will come from the details that follow, especially about the חגיגה.

keyTerms.meaning: Going up to the בית המקדש for the festival
The עולת ראייה, the שלמי חגיגה, and the שלמי שמחה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: as it was taught in a ברייתא,
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
Israel were commanded three מצוות
when they went up for the festival:
the appearance offering, the festival offering, and rejoicing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources for the תמיד view, now for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the עולה at סיני was the תמיד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי about the three festival מצוות.

steps.title: Each of the three has something special; the ראייה goes entirely to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says each of the three מצוות has a feature the other two lack. He starts with ראייה: it is burned completely on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ראייה has something the other two lack, the חגיגה has something the other two lack, and the שמחה has something the other two lack. What the ראייה has: it goes up entirely to ה׳, which is not true of the other two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up a pattern: each מצוה has one unique feature. It then explains the first one, the ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראייה is an עולה, so it is burned completely. חגיגה and שמחה are שלמים, which are mostly eaten. This feature is just part of the list; the key point for סיני comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not in the other two
Goes up entirely to ה׳ (burned completely)

phrases.english: There is something in the appearance offering that is not in the other two;
and there is something in the festival offering that is not in the other two;
there is something in the rejoicing offering that is not in the other two.
There is something in the appearance offering that is not in the other two:
that the appearance offering goes up entirely to ה׳,
which is not so with the other two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי by giving each מצוה's unique feature, starting with ראייה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three festival מצוות has a unique feature. The ראייה is unique because it is burned completely.

steps.title: Only the חגיגה existed before the דיבור at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The חגיגה's unique feature is that it existed before the דיבור at סיני, which is not true of the other two. This implies the ראייה was not offered at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חגיגה has something the other two lack: the חגיגה existed before the Divine speech at סיני, which is not true of the other two.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line for the proof. The ברייתא says only the חגיגה was brought before מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the חגיגה existed before the דיבור, then the ראייה did not. So the עולה offered at סיני could not have been an עולת ראייה. It must have been the עולת תמיד, which is why רבי יוסי הגלילי belongs in this list.

keyTerms.meaning: It exists / it was already in practice
Before the Divine speech (מתן תורה at סיני)

phrases.english: There is something in the festival offering that is not in the other two,
that the festival offering existed before the Divine speech,
phrases.notes: "The דיבור" is ה׳ speaking at הר סיני. The שלמים brought there count as a חגיגה.

phrases.english: which is not so with the other two.

steps.whyThisMatters: This one detail is the whole reason the ברייתא proves רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. Since the ראייה did not exist before the דיבור, the עולה at סיני must have been the תמיד.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says "תמיד" in this line. The proof is an inference: since there was no ראייה before the דיבור, the עולה at סיני must have been the תמיד.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second unique feature in the ברייתא. This is the feature that proves the point about סיני.
steps.raayaObject: That for רבי יוסי הגלילי the עולה at סיני was the תמיד, not a ראייה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement that only the חגיגה existed before the דיבור.

steps.title: The שמחה applies to both men and women
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. The שמחה is unique because it applies to men and women, unlike the other two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שמחה has something the other two lack: it applies to both men and women, which is not true of the other two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא completes its three-part list with the special feature of the שמחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of rejoicing on the רגל includes women too, while ראייה and חגיגה apply only to men. This finishes the ברייתא; the proof for סיני already came from the חגיגה line.

keyTerms.meaning: Applies / is practiced
With men and with women

phrases.english: There is something in the rejoicing offering that is not in the other two,
that rejoicing applies to men and to women,
which is not so with the other two.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי teaches that only the חגיגה existed before the דיבור. So the ראייה was not offered at סיני, and the עולה there was the תמיד, just as בית הלל and רבי עקיבא hold.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part list in the ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שמחה is unique because it applies to both men and women.

steps.title: Why was רבי ישמעאל grouped with בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason רבי ישמעאל was placed with בית שמאי on the question of the עולה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי ישמעאל, why did you place him with בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of opinions and asks why רבי ישמעאל was counted with בית שמאי. This sets up the next step, where the reason is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ישמעאל was counted among those who hold the עולה at סיני was an עולת ראייה, like בית שמאי. Now the גמרא wants to know what that grouping was based on, so it can check whether it holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
You established him (placed his view) as following
The school of שמאי

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael, what is the reason
that you placed him in line with Beis Shammai?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why did we say רבי ישמעאל agrees the עולה at סיני was an עולת ראייה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, מַאי טַעְמָא קָא מוֹקְמַתְּ לֵיהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי to re-examine the grouping of רבי ישמעאל made in steps 1-2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the basis for placing רבי ישמעאל with בית שמאי?

steps.title: The reasoning: an offering cannot change its rules
steps.stepSummary: If the עולה at סיני were a תמיד, it would have started without skinning and cutting and later needed it. That seemed impossible, so it must have been a different offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the עולה Israel offered in the desert was the daily עולת תמיד, is there anything that at first did not need skinning and cutting, and later did need it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the grouping. A קרבן should not first skip הפשט וניתוח and later need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that the details, like skinning and cutting, were taught only later at the אהל מועד. So the עולה at סיני had no הפשט וניתוח. If it were the תמיד, the same תמיד would later need it, which seemed odd. So it was assumed he holds it was an עולת ראייה, a one-time offering.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
The daily burnt-offering
Skinning the animal and cutting it into pieces
At first / in the end

phrases.english: If it would enter your mind
that the burnt-offering Israel offered in the desert
was the daily burnt-offering,
is there anything
that at first did not need skinning and cutting,
and in the end did need skinning and cutting?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ עוֹלָה שֶׁהִקְרִיבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר עוֹלַת תָּמִיד הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by restating the reasoning given in step 2, so that it can be tested next.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same offering, the תמיד, cannot go from not needing הפשט וניתוח to needing it, so the עולה at סיני must have been an עולת ראייה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds exactly that
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reasoning: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the עולה at סיני was the תמיד, and that it first did not need skinning and cutting but later did.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said the עולה Israel offered in the desert was the עולת תמיד. At first it did not need skinning and cutting, and later it did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reasoning from the last step. There is a תנא who openly holds the very thing that was called impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 13 depended on the idea that an offering's rules cannot change. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds they can: the תמיד at סיני had no הפשט וניתוח, and later it did. So that reasoning does not force רבי ישמעאל to agree with בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But there is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who said:
The burnt-offering Israel offered in the desert
was the daily burnt-offering;
at first it did not need skinning and cutting,
and in the end it did need skinning and cutting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an offering cannot change from not needing הפשט וניתוח to needing it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known תנא holds exactly that change happened, so it is not impossible.

steps.title: The ברייתא that shows רבי יוסי הגלילי's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי: the desert עולה did not need skinning and cutting, since that rule only started from the אהל מועד onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the עולה Israel offered in the desert did not need skinning and cutting, because skinning and cutting only applied from the אהל מועד onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting the actual ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason: the rule of הפשט וניתוח was only given at the אהל מועד. So the same תמיד offered before that time had no such rule. This proves the rules of one offering can change over time.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires
The Tent of Meeting (the משכן)
And onward

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
The burnt-offering Israel offered in the desert
does not require skinning and cutting,
because there is no skinning and cutting
except from the Tent of Meeting and onward!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the challenge in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the desert תמיד had no הפשט וניתוח, but later it did.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: Take רבי ישמעאל off the list
steps.stepSummary: Since the reasoning does not hold, the גמרא removes רבי ישמעאל from the list of those who hold like בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Remove רבי ישמעאל from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that we cannot say for sure that רבי ישמעאל holds like בית שמאי, so his name is removed from that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason for placing him with בית שמאי was the idea that rules cannot change. רבי יוסי הגלילי shows they can. So רבי ישמעאל could just as well hold the עולה was the תמיד, and he is taken off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove from here (take this out)

steps.whatToRemember: Grouping רבי ישמעאל with בית שמאי relied on the idea that an offering's rules cannot change. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds they did change, so רבי ישמעאל is taken off the list.

phrases.english: Remove Rabbi Yishmael from here.
phrases.notes: He means: take רבי ישמעאל off the list of those who say the עולה at סיני was an עולת ראייה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the successful challenge in steps 14-15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ישמעאל is no longer counted as holding like בית שמאי.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks: which animals were offered at סיני?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks how to read the פסוק: were the עולות sheep and only the שלמים bulls, or were both bulls?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked: How should this פסוק be read? "He sent the young men of Israel and they brought up burnt-offerings" were sheep, and "they sacrificed peace-offerings to ה׳" were the "bulls"? Or maybe both the עולות and the שלמים were bulls?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a new question about the פסוק describing the offerings at סיני. He asks which offerings the word "bulls" describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פרים comes at the very end of the פסוק. It could describe only the שלמים, leaving the עולות as sheep. Or it could describe both the עולות and the שלמים. The question here is how the words of the פסוק connect.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he could not settle)
How is it written? (how should it be read?)
Bulls
Sheep
Both this and that

phrases.english: Rav Chisda asked:
This verse, how is it written?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we read it? Which words go together?

phrases.english: "And he sent the young men of the children of Israel,
and they brought up burnt-offerings": these were sheep;
"And they sacrificed peace-offerings to ה׳": these were "bulls."
Or perhaps:
both of them were bulls.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב חִסְדָּא: הַאי קְרָא הֵיכִי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the same פסוק of the offerings at סיני.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "פרים" in the פסוק describe only the שלמים, or both the עולות and the שלמים?

steps.title: What difference does the reading make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes whether only the שלמים were bulls or the עולות were bulls too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא's question matters at all. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offerings at סיני were brought long ago, so knowing which animals were used seems to have no practical use. The גמרא wants to know where the difference actually shows up.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical use there is in the question raised in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical result depends on whether the עולות at סיני were bulls or sheep.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: it affects the trope of the verse
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the difference is in where the trope marks place the pause in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The difference is in how the trope notes divide the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers that the difference is in how we read the פסוק out loud, meaning where the trope marks put the break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the שלמים were bulls, the פסוק pauses after "they brought עולות." If both were bulls, the word "bulls" goes with both, so the whole phrase is read as one unit with no break.

keyTerms.meaning: How the trope marks divide a פסוק into parts

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
For the division of the cantillation notes.
phrases.notes: The טעמים are the trope marks. They show where you pause when reading the פסוק (שמות 24:5).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is in where the trope marks place the break in the פסוק.

steps.title: רב אחא: it affects a vow to bring an offering like the desert one
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says the difference is for someone who vows to bring an עולה like the one Israel brought in the desert. Must he bring a bull or a sheep?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said: The difference is for someone who says, "I take on myself to bring an עולה like the עולה that Israel brought in the desert." What must he bring? Were they bulls, or were they sheep?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא gives a practical, הלכה-based difference. It affects what a person must bring if he vowed an עולה "like the one in the desert."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר is measured by what the person said. If the desert עולות were bulls, he must bring a bull. If they were sheep, a sheep is enough. So the reading of the פסוק decides what he owes.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is upon me": the wording of a vow to bring an offering
Bulls
Sheep (lambs)

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said:
For one who says: "It is upon me to bring a burnt-offering
like the burnt-offering that Israel brought in the desert,"
what is the law? Were they bulls,
or were they sheep?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר: לָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to Step 18. This one has a practical result in הלכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is what animal a person must bring if he vowed an עולה like the one in the desert.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide whether the desert עולות were bulls or sheep, so the question stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with תיקו. The question of whether the עולות were bulls or sheep stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles how to read the פסוק. So both רב חסדא's question and its practical result for the vow stay open.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let it stand": the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: We do not know whether the עולות at סיני were bulls or sheep. This affects the trope of the פסוק and what a person must bring if he vows an עולה like the one in the desert.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in Steps 17 and 20 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reading of the פסוק, and so the law of the vow, stays undecided.

steps.title: A משנה in פאה: things with no set measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a משנה from מסכת פאה that lists מצוות with no fixed measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: These are the things that have no set measure:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It starts quoting a משנה from מסכת פאה, setting up a discussion about מצוות that have no fixed amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "There" means another מסכת, here פאה. The list of things with no measure is quoted next. It includes the ראיון, the festival appearance that this מסכת deals with.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed measure or amount

phrases.english: We learned there, in a mishna:
phrases.notes: "There" is מסכת פאה, at the very start of the first פרק.

phrases.english: These are the things that have no measure:

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם, אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion that has nothing to do with the question about the offerings at סיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some מצוות have no fixed measure (the list follows).
